articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly's Darius Cooper.

The scoring picked up in the late window Sunday, as the Cowboys and Commanders combined for 57 points. However, Washington lost QB Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury in the second quarter -- hours after Chicago lost QB Caleb Williams to a right hamstring injury. Meanwhile, the 49ers dominated the Dolphins in their first game back from Melbourne, Australia. And the Seahawks won their second straight game with backup quarterback Drew Lock.

The night game featured a wild ending, but ultimately the Kansas City Chiefs improved to 2-0 with an overtime thriller over the Indianapolis Colts.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Chiefs

Did Patrick Mahomes' performance demonstrate the Chiefs are back as contenders? That appears to be the case after two weeks. In overtime, Mahomes orchestrated the 25th game-winning drive of his 10-year career, which is tied with Kirk Cousins for second-most in that span. Last season, the Chiefs were bad in one-score games, finishing with a 1-9 record. Mahomes, though, proved he's capable of carrying the Chiefs yet again to another dramatic win. In just his second game after recovering from the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, Mahomes was heroic, finishing with 382 passing yards and three touchdowns without committing a turnover.

Most surprising performance: Of course, Mahomes spent most of Sunday relying on tight end Travis Kelce, who led the Chiefs with 101 receiving yards and a touchdown. Yet receiver Tyquan Thornton was just as impactful for the Chiefs offense. At pivotal moments, Thornton was impressive in catching all four of his targets for 86 yards, including a 45-yard reception. That highlight was the first time in the game that the Chiefs offense converted on third down. -- Nate Taylor

articles.headline: Week 2 winners and losers: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb shine; Bijan Robinson struggles
articles.description: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and CeeDee Lamb came up big in Week 2, while Bijan Robinson and Justin Jefferson had very quiet days.
articles.body:
Week 2 of the 2026 fantasy football season wasn't the high-scoring bonanza of Week 1, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith all came up big. On the flip side, fantasy stars Bijan Robinson, Justin Jefferson and Drake London all had disappointing games.

Who were the big winners and losers around the league during the second week of the fantasy football season?

Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.

Jump to a topic:

Ranking winners | Ranking losers 

Biggest injuries and what's next

Ranking fantasy winners of Week 2

1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

After a stellar, breakthrough 2025 that saw him score the second-most fantasy points among wide receivers, it might be shocking to learn that this week's 42.5 points set Smith-Njigba's new personal best. He flashed good chemistry with fill-in quarterback Drew Lock and was productive at all levels of the field. This was vintage JSN, and we should see something similar in a great Week 3 matchup against the Washington Commanders. -- Cockcroft

2. Dak Prescott, QB, CeeDee Lamb, WR, and Jake Ferguson, TE, Dallas Cowboys

In a positive matchup versus the Commanders, the Cowboys had multiple Week 2 winners. Prescott had 29.76 points, attacking every level of the field in the pass game, finishing with 279 yards and four touchdowns, while adding 26 yards on the ground. Lamb's 35.3 points were the second most among wide receivers through the late window. Lamb caught 8 of 9 targets for 153 yards and added two scores. And don't forget about Ferguson in scoring position. The tight end caught all four of his targets for 43 yards, with two touchdown grabs on red zone throws (20.3 points). Because of his red zone usage, Ferguson will stay in the lower-tier TE1 mix for the Week 3 matchup versus Baltimore. -- Bowen

3. DeVonta Smith, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

If he's destined for a breakout, fantasy WR1-caliber year, this might well be the starting-point game his managers refer to. Smith scored 27.7 fantasy points, his sixth most in 82 career games, and he had a 38% target share. He's in prime position to shine, with A.J. Brown now in New England, and he'll get a fantastic Week 3 matchup in which to potentially repeat the effort versus the Chicago Bears. -- Cockcroft

4. Tyler Shough, QB, and Chris Olave, WR, New Orleans Saints

The Shough-Olave combination produced high-end numbers again in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. Shough (22.38 points) threw for 252 yards and a touchdown, while he rushed for 23 yards and another score on nine carries. That's two straight games for Shough with at least 22 points. Olave caught 8 of a team-high 10 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown, which was good for 22.6 points -- after dropping 28.2 points on the Lions in Week 1. Olave will remain a midtier WR1 for me in the ranks for the Week 3 matchup versus the Raiders, while Shough should be viewed as a fringe QB1. -- Bowen

5. Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Cincinnati Bengals

articles.headline: Mahomes and Walker shine, Butker hits winning 40-yarder as Chiefs beat Colts 33-30 in OT
articles.description: — Harrison Butker kicked two field goals in overtime, the second a 40-yarder as time expired that Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III set up, giving the Kansas City Chiefs a 33-30 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — Harrison Butker kicked two field goals in overtime, the second a 40-yarder as time expired that Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III set up, giving the Kansas City Chiefs a 33-30 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night.


              Mahomes finished with 382 yards passing and three touchdowns, Walker ran for 117 yards, and Travis Kelce looked like a younger version of himself with nine catches for 101 yards and a score as the Chiefs improved to 2-0.


              Daniel Jones had 210 yards passing with a touchdown and a pick for the Colts. Jonathan Taylor had 92 yards rushing and two TDs.


              The Chiefs thought they had won the game earlier in overtime on a bizarre sequence of events.


              Butker kicked a 31-yard field goal to give them the lead, and the Colts (0-2) responded on their possession by having Jones throw deep to Laquon Treadwell, who had beaten L'Jarius Snead. Treadwell appeared to be bobbling the ball as he hit the ground, got up after he had completed the catch, had the ball popped loose and watched as the Chiefs pounced on it.


              The play was ruled a fumble on the field, but the officials reviewed it and determined Treadwell was down by contact. That gave the Colts a chance to score a go-ahead touchdown, but they ended up having to settle for Spencer Shrader's tying 38-yard field goal.


              The Chiefs took over once more with 3:11 left in the extra session, and they handed off to Walker on three straight plays to reach midfield. But the backbreaker for Indianapolis was a 22-yard pass to the running back, which set up Butker's winning kick.


              The Colts had chalked up a disastrous defensive performance against Baltimore in Week 1 to communication problems, and they hoped to solve them by having linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither relay the play calls rather than safety Cam Bynum. But the tweak didn’t seem to make much difference as Kansas City was marched up and down the field throughout the game.


              Each of the Chiefs’ first four drives would have produced points had Butker not missed a 51-yard field goal try.


              Yet the Colts were able to match Mahomes and Co. blow-for-blow over the first 30 minutes. Tyler Warren had three catches and a touchdown, Josh Downs picked apart a Chiefs secondary missing safety Chamarri Conner for a second straight game, and Taylor had 75 of his rushing yards — the highlight a 24-yard touchdown scamper that gave Indianapolis a 20-17 lead at the break.


              The Chiefs allowed Denver to run for just 61 yards total in their 31-10 win last week.


              Kansas City finally slowed the Colts’ offense by refusing to give them the ball. The Chiefs held it for all but 2:22 of the third quarter, getting a go-ahead TD pass to Jalen Royals and setting up Butker’s field goal to start the fourth.

articles.headline: Brewers savor franchise-record 98th victory as playoffs loom
articles.description: Milwaukee broke the single-season wins mark it set last season Sunday night, smothering Baltimore 3-0 to improve to 98-58.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- The Milwaukee Brewers haven't won more than five games in a row all year. It hasn't stopped them from setting a single-season franchise record for victories.

Milwaukee broke the mark it set last season Sunday night, smothering the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 to improve to 98-58.

"We haven't had these streaks of greatness," manager Pat Murphy said. "We haven't put it all together."

Even without rattling off an extended run, the Brewers have the best record in the majors. They've already clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central title and will make their eighth postseason appearance in nine years. Twice in that span they've advanced to the NL Championship Series, including last year, but they have not reached the World Series since 1982.

Milwaukee completed its ninth series sweep of the season while receiving help from all over the roster. The Brewers stole four bases, got a stellar diving catch from center fielder Garrett Mitchell in the seventh inning and had seven pitchers combine on a four-hit shutout for the record-setting victory with six games left.

"It means a lot," said pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (15-5, 1.86 ERA), who gave up a hit and struck out four in three innings in an abbreviated start designed to manage his workload.

"It's always a big deal to set a new record, a franchise record at that. Hopefully, we get a few more and get to a little bigger number."

Milwaukee enters the final week of the season two games ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers for the best record in the NL and needs only one more victory or an Atlanta loss to lock up a bye into the division series.

"It's hard to be in this spot to begin with, and I don't think it's appreciated enough," Murphy said. "I think people don't realize how hard it is for any of the 30 teams to put themselves in this position, and that's what makes me proud of these guys. We're not the oldest team, we're not the most experienced, we're not the most talented. We're not the most a lot of things, but for sure they've proven they're a team."

articles.headline: Who are the winningest NFL coaches of all time?
articles.description: From Belichick to Reid, there are many iconic coaches in NFL history. Who has the best career record? Check out the stat breakdown now.
articles.body:
Only four head coaches in NFL history have won 300 career games across the regular season and postseason. Kansas City Chiefs coach Andy Reid was the last to cross the 300-win plateau.

Reid recorded his 300th career victory on Jan. 18, 2025, when his Chiefs defeated the Houston Texans 23-14 in the AFC divisional round.

Reid, who signed a five-year, $100 million extension with the Chiefs in April 2024, entered the 2026 season looking to add to his career win total and close the gap between him and the NFL's all-time winningest head coach, Hall of Famer Don Shula.

Let's take a look at which head coaches have the most career victories in NFL history (including both regular-season and postseason play):

*Active NFL head coach

5. Tom Landry, 270 wins

Landry was the Dallas Cowboys' head coach for an NFL-record 29 years in a row and the team had 20 consecutive winning seasons, which is also a league record. Landry led Dallas to two Super Bowl wins, defeating the Miami Dolphins in Super Bowl VI and the Denver Broncos in Super Bowl XII. He was named the NFL's Coach of the Year in 1966 and the UPI NFL Coach of the Year in 1975. Landry was an innovator, with the 4-3 defense among his creations. He was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

*4. Andy Reid, 309 wins

Reid is the only head coach in NFL history who has won 100 games with two franchises: the Philadelphia Eagles (coaching the team from 1999 through 2012) and the Chiefs (he has coached Kansas City since 2013). He led the Eagles on multiple deep playoff runs, including a Super Bowl in 2004 and three straight conference finals from 2001 to 2003. However, he wasn't able to hoist the Lombardi Trophy until he arrived in Kansas City. He has turned the Chiefs into a juggernaut, winning three Super Bowls. Reid is an offensive mastermind and quarterback whisperer. He'll likely continue to rack up wins moving forward with Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce & Co.

3. George Halas, 324 wins

Halas was a co-founder of the NFL and creator of the Bears. For 10 years, he served as player-coach-executive for the Bears (which is how he earned the nickname "Mr. Everything"). In 1930, he retired as a player and focused on ownership, but he would later return to coach the Bears several times. Halas led the Bears to eight NFL championships, tying Belichick's number of titles. Halas coached the team for 40 years and had just six losing seasons. He helped create the T-formation system and used it to set an NFL record for the biggest blowout in league history: a 73-0 win over the Washington team in the 1940 NFL Championship Game. Halas was selected as the AP's NFL Coach of the Year in 1963 and 1965, and he was named to the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team.

2. Bill Belichick, 333 wins

articles.headline: Lock, Smith-Njigba have Seahawks 2-0 with Darnold ahead of schedule
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold could return to practice this week and did not rule out the possibility of him playing next Sunday. In the meantime, backup Drew Lock has Seattle 2-0, with plenty of help from receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
articles.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- The Seattle Seahawks might get Sam Darnold back from his glute injury sooner than they initially expected. Coach Mike Macdonald said postgame Sunday that the quarterback's timetable has "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Darnold could return to practice sometime this week, and after the Seahawks improved to 2-0 with a 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium, Macdonald didn't rule out Seattle's QB1 possibly playing next Sunday against the Washington Commanders (0-2).

Though Drew Lock's hot start to the season could give the Seahawks reason to take their time with Darnold, Macdonald insisted that the decision will be based on his readiness.

"If Sam can play, he's going to play," Macdonald said. "If Sam can't play, then Drew will play. It's pretty simple."

In the meantime, Lock is playing starter-level football, and he's getting plenty of help from Jaxon Smith-Njigba as well as last season's top-ranked scoring defense. Lock threw three more touchdown passes to the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year on Sunday, and Macdonald's unit shut the door in the second half to turn a 7-7 score into a runaway victory.

In his first start since 2024, Lock completed 19 of 26 attempts for 235 yards and no interceptions. As he mostly did last week in helping rally the Seahawks to a season-opening win over the New England Patriots after Darnold went down on the game's fifth play, Lock kept the ball out of harm's way against Arizona, and he was sacked only once.

"Really proud of Drew, really happy for him," Macdonald said. "We're on the record in how we feel about him, so he just backed that up today. That's a 12 as one thing, everybody having each other's back. You just couldn't be happier for the guy. We just love him. All the things we said about him throughout the week, that was real. That was from the heart. Really proud of the way he played today. He did a tremendous job."

Lock's first touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba came on their second play from scrimmage, when the receiver used a head fake to get wide open behind Arizona's defense for an 82-yard score. They connected for a 7-yard touchdown in the third quarter and a 12-yarder in the fourth, both coming on third down.

Lock's lone touchdown pass in the opener was to Smith-Njigba.

"We've been having a special connection for a minute now, but I'm super happy [for] the way he just came in and carried himself and carried this team," Smith-Njigba said of Lock. "He shows time and time again how good he is."

Per ESPN Research, Smith-Njigba is the third player in franchise history with 150-plus receiving yards and three receiving TDs in a game, joining Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent (twice). Smith-Njigba now has an NFL-high 11 games with at least 100 receiving yards since the start of last season. He's the first Seahawk to catch three touchdown passes in a game since DK Metcalf in 2023.
